**What:** the owner's personal portfolio and resume site, live at vijeth-portfolio.pages.dev
(the sister tool sites link to it from their About pages).
**Stack:** Astro (static) + Tailwind CSS 4. Deployed to the Cloudflare Pages project

npm run dev

npm run deploy    # astro build && wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name vijeth-portfolio

Commit all (common §2) → `git push origin master` → `npm run deploy` → `curl -sI` the live URL.
No IndexNow here.

## 2. Permission to act: commit, push, deploy

- **Never commit, push or deploy unless the owner asks** in this conversation ("commit",
  "push", "deploy", "ship it"). Finish the work, report it, and stop.
- "commit" means **stage every change in the repo**, including files left over from earlier
  sessions (the owner often continues across sessions). Run `git status` first. Leave out only
  the local-only files in §3. After `git add -A`, run `git status` again and unstage anything
  from §3 before committing.
- "push, commit and deploy" (or "deploy") means: commit → push → ship the way the table in §1
  says → confirm it is live → **IndexNow** (tool sites). IndexNow is part of every deploy by
  default; never ask about it.
- Keep unrelated changes in **separate commits** (e.g. a `.gitattributes` change gets its own
  one-line commit and does not go into a feature diff).
- Commit messages: one plain sentence saying what changed for the user, such as
  `Fix °C landing routes, breadcrumbs and sitemap dates`. No "WIP" and no "update files".
- Never force-push, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, rewrite history, or delete branches unless
  the owner asks for that exact action.
- Before you say "pushed", check that it worked: `git status` shows nothing to commit and
  `git log origin/<branch> -1` matches your commit. If one file was left out, say so (this has
  happened before: "one file is still not committed and pushed").

## 3. Local-only files: never commit, push or deploy these

- `competitor-analysis.md` / `COMPETITOR-ANALYSIS.md`. They are gitignored on purpose and their
  header says "Local reference only. Do not commit or publish." Read and update them locally,
  but **never `git add -f` them**.
- `manuals/`, `scratch/` (downloaded manufacturer PDFs), `*.dc.html` plan files,
  `Embed Route Decision*`, `.dev.vars`, `.env*`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`.
- When a file's own header says "do not commit", follow the header even if git history shows it
  was committed before.
- **Do not send repo contents or files to any outside URL.** The owner has asked for this
  explicitly. Allowed outbound calls are the project's own deploy (wrangler / git push),
  IndexNow (URL list only), and fetching public pages to read them.

## 4. How the owner hands you work

- The **prompt queue lives in the project's `competitor-analysis.md`** (airfryertoolkit:
  Section 10; the current prompt is in 10.0 and shipped summaries go in the 10.1 "Shipped log".
  imagetoolkit: the "Next-build prompt" block just above Section 10 Change Log). When the owner
  says "next prompt added", "prompt is in the file" or "your prompt starts from line N", open that
  file and read **from that exact line**. Don't pick an older block that has already shipped.
- Read the project's **Section 0 (build guide) and its definition of done** before you build
  anything.
- If the prompt says **"STOP AND ASK"**, propose your answer and wait. Write no code before the
  owner approves. Once they approve, do the whole job in one go: build, verify, report.
- Pasted messages that start with "Approved, with these changes" are binding specs. Do every
  numbered item. In your report, go item by item and say what you did for each.
- When a round is done: update the doc's tracker or shipped log, mark rows ✅ with the date, and
  bump the doc's "Last updated" date.

## 5. Verification and reporting

- **Nothing counts as "passed" without a number.** Report the counts, for example
  "astro check 0 errors · build OK · e2e 612 passed, 1 skipped · test:urls 410 passed".
- Run the project's full gate before any push (each project section lists it). If a test fails,
  report the output. Never weaken or delete a test to make it pass.
- Add tests that would have caught the bug you fixed (sitemap parses, every URL returns 200,
  canonicals point to themselves, engine numbers come from the engine).
- After a deploy, **check the live site**: `curl -sI` the changed URLs (200, no redirect chain),
  check that `sitemap.xml` parses, and check the new pages are in the sitemap. Then run IndexNow
  and report how many URLs it submitted.
- Don't state search results, rankings or traffic you haven't fetched. Rankings come **only from
  Search Console**. Only cite numbers you have read in an official source. If you can't verify
  a value, say so. Don't invent one.
- If an action is blocked (by a permission prompt, the classifier or a missing login), say
  exactly which command was blocked and why. Don't claim it ran.

## 7. Windows machine gotchas (cost real time before)

- The path contains a space: always quote `"D:\Part time\SaaS\..."` (Git Bash:
  `"/d/Part time/SaaS/..."`).
- **`git` says "dubious ownership"** in `quickmeasuretool` / `portfolio` because the folders were
  moved from `D:\SaaS`. The owner fixes this once, by running
  `git config --global --add safe.directory "D:/Part time/SaaS/<project>"`. For a read-only check
  you can use `git -c safe.directory="*" ...`.
- Stopping `wrangler dev` leaves `workerd.exe` and wrangler `node` processes alive. They lock
  `dist/`, and the next `astro build` fails with a misleading "options.recursive is no longer
  supported" error. Kill them first:
  `Get-Process workerd -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force`, plus any node process whose
  command line contains `wrangler`.
- `astro build` sometimes prints "Complete!" and then a libuv `UV_HANDLE_CLOSING` assertion.
  The build still succeeded, so rerun only the step after it.
- Memory is tight. Claude Code may kill an idle dev server or test run with a "low memory" note.
  Don't restart it on your own; report it. Run one Playwright suite at a time.
- Astro 6 + `@tailwindcss/vite`: pin `"vite": "^7.3.2"` (and `tailwindcss` /
  `@tailwindcss/vite` `4.3.0`) or npm pulls vite 8 and the build breaks.
- `npx wrangler types` crashes on this machine. Bindings are declared by hand in `env.d.ts`.

## 8. Content and SEO rules shared by the tool sites

- Every page passes `title`, `description` and `canonical` to `<Layout>`. Tool pages also carry
  **WebApplication + FAQPage** JSON-LD (BreadcrumbList where the project uses it), using
  `<script type="application/ld+json" is:inline>`.
- Canonical URLs have **no trailing slash**. The slashed form must return exactly one 301/308,
  never a 307 or a chain.
- The sitemap is **generated** (`src/pages/sitemap.xml.ts`). Never create a static
  `public/sitemap.xml`. After adding pages, resubmit the sitemap in Search Console when asked.
- Thin-content guardrail: 500–600 words per page minimum, with a distinct worked example, a
  distinct FAQ, and a real reason for the page to exist. **Overlap check first:** grep for the
  target keyword. If an existing page already answers it, expand that page instead of adding a URL.
- No emoji in the UI (SVG marks only). No interstitials or newsletter popups. Ads only in dead
  zones, never over or above the tool. `<AdSlot>` handles its own "no ads yet" guard.
- Mobile: test at 375px and 412–430px, with tap targets of 44px or more.
- When you change a backend (email, storage, third-party service), grep the whole repo for the
  old name. Privacy and terms pages describe implementation details and go stale without
  warning.
